mainTopic: When a large קרפף counts as enclosed for living: sown or planted areas, rebuilding the wall, doorways, and flooding
overview: This amud opens at the end of a challenge about a large קרפף whose majority was sown with seeds. The small unsown part is בטל to the sown majority, so the whole area becomes a forbidden קרפף larger than בית סאתים. The גמרא therefore restates the ruling: a sown minority is permitted. רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע limits this by size, and his limit comes in two versions. One version matches the רבנן and the other matches רבי שמעון. Next, אבימי and רב נחמן argue over whether a קרפף mostly planted with trees counts as a חצר only when the trees stand in rows, and a story shows רב הונא בר יהודה following רב נחמן. שמואל then teaches how to fix a large קרפף not enclosed for living: break more than ten אמות of the wall and rebuild it down to ten. The גמרא asks whether doing this one אמה at a time works, and settles it through חזקיה's question about small sealed holes and רבי יוחנן's proof from a sandal: 'פנים חדשות באו לכאן.' The amud ends with three rulings: רב כהנא on a רחבה behind houses, רב נחמן on a doorway opened before the fence, and רבא's ruling that a flooded קרפף is like one planted with trees, so carrying stays permitted.

steps.title: The small unsown part gets swallowed by the sown majority
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes its challenge to the earlier version of the ruling: the minority is בטל to the majority, so the whole קרפף counts as more than בית סאתים and carrying is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: The minority part is nullified relative to the majority, so it becomes a קרפף larger than בית סאתים, and carrying is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a challenge to an earlier version of a ruling about a קרפף where most of the area was sown with seeds. It argues that the leftover unsown part simply joins the sown majority, so the whole area is forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Land sown with seeds (זרעים) is not used for living, so it is not treated as 'fenced for dwelling.' If most of the קרפף is sown, the small unsown part is בטל to it, and the whole area counts as sown. The result is a קרפף larger than בית סאתים that was not fenced for dwelling, and carrying in it is אסור. This forces the גמרא to reformulate the ruling in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Nullified; a small part loses its own identity and is absorbed into the larger part
An enclosed open area behind houses, such as a storage yard
An area where two סאה of seed can be sown, about 5,000 square אמות. This is the size limit for carrying in a קרפף not fenced for dwelling

steps.confusionAlert: This amud starts in the middle of the גמרא's argument. The line here is the END of a challenge to an earlier version of the ruling. It is not a new rule.

phrases.english: it (the minority) is nullified relative to the majority,
phrases.notes: The unsown minority is absorbed into the sown majority.

phrases.aramaic: וְהָוֵה לֵיהּ קַרְפֵּף יוֹתֵר מִבֵּית סָאתַיִם — וְאָסוּר.
phrases.english: and it becomes a karpef larger than two beit se'a, and it is forbidden.
phrases.notes: The whole area is now treated as planted, not as fenced for dwelling.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the challenge earlier (end of 23b) against the earlier version of the ruling.
steps.kashyaTarget: The earlier version of the ruling about a קרפף whose majority was sown
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Because of ביטול, the minority joins the sown majority. That turns the entire area into a forbidden קרפף larger than בית סאתים, so the earlier version cannot stand.

steps.title: Restating the ruling: a sown minority is permitted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reformulates the ruling: a sown majority forbids carrying, which implies that a sown minority permits it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, if this was said, this is how it was said: from the ruling about a sown majority we learn that a sown minority is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by rewording the original statement. Carrying is forbidden only when the majority is sown, so when only a minority is sown, carrying is allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase אלא אי איתמר הכי איתמר tells us the earlier quote was inaccurate and replaces it. Now the logic of ביטול works in our favor. A small sown part is swallowed up by the larger dwelling area, so the קרפף keeps its permitted status.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, if it was stated, it was stated like this. Used to correct a quote

steps.whyThisMatters: The same principle of ביטול that knocked down the old version now supports the new version, just in the opposite direction.

phrases.english: Rather, if it was stated, this is how it was stated:
it follows that a minority (sown) is permitted.
phrases.notes: We learn this from the rule that a sown majority is forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge of step 1 by rewording the ruling.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The earlier version of the ruling, which could not survive the ביטול argument
steps.terutzMaskana: A sown majority forbids carrying. A sown minority is permitted.

steps.title: Strict limit: a sown area of exactly בית סאתים already forbids
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע limits the leniency: a sown minority is permitted only if it is smaller than בית סאתים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע said: we only permitted it when the sown part is not as big as בית סאתים. But if the sown part is בית סאתים, it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע adds a size limit to the leniency of a sown minority. Even a minority can forbid carrying if it reaches the size of בית סאתים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A sown area of בית סאתים is big enough to count as its own separate area. It is not simply swallowed up as a minority. So even though most of the קרפף is not sown, a sown section of a full בית סאתים forbids carrying in the whole area.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא, son of רב יהושע
We only said this when, introducing a limitation

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ:
phrases.english: Rav Huna, son of Rav Yehoshua, said:

phrases.aramaic: לָא אֲמַרַן אֶלָּא דְּלָא הָוֵי בֵּית סָאתַיִם,
phrases.english: We said this only when it (the sown part) is not two beit se'a,
but if it is two beit se'a, it is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא אֲמַרַן אֶלָּא דְּלָא הָוֵי בֵּית סָאתַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the leniency stated in step 2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A sown minority is permitted only if it is less than בית סאתים. A sown area of exactly בית סאתים forbids carrying.

steps.title: Whose view does the strict limit follow?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which תנא this strict limit matches.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to whom?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which earlier opinion the strict version of רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע's limit follows. This is a setup question, and the answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a request for information, not an attack. The גמרא wants to link the limit to a known מחלוקת so we understand why the line is drawn at exactly בית סאתים.

keyTerms.meaning: According to whom? Which opinion does this follow?

phrases.english: According to whom?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source opinion behind step 3.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא's view is the basis for forbidding a sown area of exactly בית סאתים

steps.title: It follows the רבנן
steps.stepSummary: The strict limit follows the רבנן, who treat a קרפף and a חצר as separate domains.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to the רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the strict version follows the רבנן. They disagree with רבי שמעון and hold that one may not carry between a קרפף and a חצר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to the רבנן, an area of בית סאתים is a distinct domain that does not merge with the area next to it. So a sown section of a full בית סאתים stands on its own and forbids carrying, even though it is only a minority of the קרפף.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages, the majority opinion against רבי שמעון

steps.whatToRemember: Strict version: a sown area of exactly בית סאתים already forbids carrying, which fits the רבנן.

phrases.english: According to the Rabbis.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 4.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The strict limit follows the רבנן, who hold that a קרפף and a חצר are separate domains.

steps.title: Lenient version: only more than בית סאתים forbids
steps.stepSummary: רב ירמיה מדיפתי teaches רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע's limit more leniently: a sown area of exactly בית סאתים is still permitted, and only more than that forbids.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ירמיה מדיפתי taught it leniently: a planted minority is permitted. רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע said: we only permitted it up to בית סאתים, but more than בית סאתים is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second version of the same statement, taught by רב ירמיה מדיפתי. In his version, the sown area may be as large as exactly בית סאתים, and only a sown area larger than that forbids carrying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both versions agree that a sown minority is generally permitted and that size matters. The only difference is the exact line. In the first version, exactly בית סאתים forbids. In this version, exactly בית סאתים is allowed, and only more than that forbids.

keyTerms.meaning: Rav Yirmeya from the town of Difti, an אמורא

steps.confusionAlert: This is NOT a new ruling by a different אמורא. It is the same statement of רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע, transmitted with a slightly different size limit.

phrases.english: And Rav Yirmeya from Difti taught it leniently:
it follows that a minority (sown) is permitted,

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ:
phrases.english: Rav Huna, son of Rav Yehoshua, said:
We said this only up to two beit se'a,
but more than two beit se'a is forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a competing version of the limit given in step 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A planted minority of up to exactly בית סאתים is permitted. Only a planted area larger than בית סאתים forbids carrying.

steps.title: Whose view does the lenient version follow?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא again asks which תנא this version matches.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to whom?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks the same question about the lenient version. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just as it did with the strict version, the גמרא connects the lenient line to a known opinion so we can see why the two versions draw the line in different places.

phrases.english: According to whom?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallels step 4 for the lenient version.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא's view allows a planted area of exactly בית סאתים

steps.title: It follows רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: The lenient version follows רבי שמעון, who is more lenient about carrying between a קרפף and a חצר.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to רבי שמעון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the lenient version follows רבי שמעון. He allows carrying between a קרפף and a חצר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since רבי שמעון lets a קרפף of up to בית סאתים connect with a חצר, a sown section of exactly בית סאתים does not cut itself off from the rest. Only a sown area larger than בית סאתים causes a problem. So the two versions of רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע simply reflect the מחלוקת between the רבנן and רבי שמעון.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא who is lenient about carrying between a קרפף and a חצר

steps.whatToRemember: Two versions of the same limit: the strict version (exactly בית סאתים forbids) follows the רבנן, and the lenient version (only more than בית סאתים forbids) follows רבי שמעון.

phrases.english: According to Rabbi Shimon.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 7 and completes the parallel to steps 4 and 5.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The lenient version follows רבי שמעון.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The disagreement over whether a planted area of exactly בית סאתים forbids carrying mirrors the מחלוקת between the רבנן and רבי שמעון about a קרפף and a חצר.

steps.title: Planted trees only count if they stand in rows
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes again the rule that a קרפף mostly planted with trees is like a חצר. רב יהודה, quoting אבימי, limits it to trees planted in rows.
steps.simpleTranslation: If most of it was planted with trees, it is like a courtyard and carrying is permitted. רב יהודה said in the name of אבימי: this is only when the trees are planted in rows.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings back the earlier rule about a planted קרפף so it can add a limit to it. אבימי says the trees must be set up in rows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Trees in neat rows look like the decorative planting people put in a living courtyard, so the area still looks lived-in. Trees scattered randomly look like an orchard, which is not a place people live in. So according to אבימי, only rows keep the חצר status.

keyTerms.meaning: He planted most of it with trees
Like a courtyard, a lived-in area where carrying is allowed
Neat rows of trees, the way decorative trees are planted
'This is only when…', a phrase that adds a limit to a rule

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two cases. Planting trees (נטע) keeps the area like a חצר and is permitted. Sowing seeds or crops (זרע) makes it like a vegetable garden (גינה), and carrying there is forbidden.

phrases.english: If he planted most of it [with trees]
it is like a courtyard, and it is permitted.
Rav Yehuda said in the name of Avimi:
This is only when they are planted in rows.
phrases.notes: Trees in rows look like decorative courtyard planting, not like an orchard.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר אֲבִימִי: וְהוּא שֶׁעֲשׂוּיִין אִצְטַבְּלָאוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the planted-trees part of רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע's rule and adds a limit to it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A planted קרפף counts as a חצר only when the trees are planted in rows.

steps.title: רב נחמן: rows are not needed
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן disagrees with אבימי. Even without rows, a mostly-planted קרפף is like a חצר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: even if the trees are not planted in rows.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן gives the opposite view to אבימי. Any tree planting counts, whatever the arrangement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן holds that people plant trees around their homes in all kinds of patterns. So the arrangement of the trees does not change whether the area looks lived-in.

keyTerms.meaning: Arranged or made (in a certain way)

phrases.english: But Rav Nachman said:

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין עֲשׂוּיִין אִצְטַבְּלָאוֹת.
phrases.english: even if they are not planted in rows.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב נַחְמָן אָמַר: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין עֲשׂוּיִין אִצְטַבְּלָאוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with אבימי's limit from step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A mostly-planted קרפף is like a חצר even if the trees are not in rows.

steps.title: מר יהודה sees people carrying among trees that are not in rows
steps.stepSummary: מר יהודה visits רב הונא בר יהודה and sees people carrying among trees that are not in rows. He asks whether רב הונא disagrees with אבימי.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר יהודה came to the house of רב הונא בר יהודה. He saw trees that were not planted in rows, yet people were carrying among them. He asked him: Does the Master not hold like אבימי's teaching?
steps.whatsHappening: A short story. מר יהודה sees a practice that seems to go against אבימי's ruling, and he questions רב הונא בר יהודה about it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מר יהודה assumes the halacha follows אבימי from step 9. In that case, trees that are not in rows do not give the area the status of a חצר, and carrying among them should be forbidden. His question challenges the household's practice.

keyTerms.meaning: Does the Master not hold this view?

phrases.english: Mar Yehuda happened to come
to the house of Rav Huna bar Yehuda.
He saw certain trees that were not planted in rows,
and people were carrying among them.
He said to him:

phrases.aramaic: לָא סָבַר לַהּ מָר לְהָא דַּאֲבִימִי?
phrases.english: Does the Master not hold of this teaching of Avimi?

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא סָבַר לַהּ מָר לְהָא דַּאֲבִימִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Puts the dispute from steps 9 and 10 into a real-life case.
steps.kashyaTarget: The practice of carrying among trees that are not in rows at רב הונא בר יהודה's house.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: According to אבימי, trees that are not in rows do not make the area like a חצר, so carrying there should be forbidden.

steps.title: רב הונא follows רב נחמן
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בר יהודה answers that he holds like רב נחמן, so rows are not needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: I hold like רב נחמן.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא explains his practice. He follows רב נחמן's lenient view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There was no mistake at the house. The household simply follows the other opinion. The story shows that רב נחמן's view was actually followed in practice.
steps.whatToRemember: אבימי requires the trees to be in rows. רב נחמן does not, and רב הונא בר יהודה followed רב נחמן in practice.

phrases.english: He said to him:
I hold like Rav Nachman.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers מר יהודה's challenge from step 11.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The household was carrying against the halacha, as אבימי rules.
steps.terutzMaskana: They follow רב נחמן, who does not require rows.

steps.title: How to fix a large enclosure not made for living
steps.stepSummary: שמואל teaches a fix for a קרפף larger than בית סאתים that was not enclosed for living. Break open more than ten אמות of the wall, then close it back down to ten, and carrying becomes permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said in the name of שמואל: A קרפף larger than בית סאתים that was not enclosed for living, what can one do? He breaks a gap of more than ten אמות in it, then fences it back so the gap is only ten, and it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: A new teaching. שמואל gives a practical way to make a large unlivable enclosure usable for carrying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A gap wider than ten אמות cancels the wall, so the old enclosure is gone. When he closes the gap back down to ten, the remaining opening counts as a doorway (פתח). The wall is now newly built while he lives there, so it counts as enclosed for living (לדירה).

keyTerms.meaning: Enclosed for the purpose of living there
Breaks open a gap in the wall
Reduces the opening down to ten אמות

steps.confusionAlert: Up to ten אמות is a doorway, and the wall still stands. More than ten is a breach that cancels the wall. That is why he first opens more than ten and then closes back to exactly ten.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that an enclosure's status depends on why the wall was made. Rebuilding with a new purpose can change the status.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said in the name of Shmuel:
An enclosure larger than two beit se'a
that was not enclosed for living,
what should he do?
He breaks a gap in it of more than ten [cubits],
phrases.notes: A gap this wide cancels the wall.

phrases.english: then fences it and reduces it to ten,
phrases.notes: An opening of ten counts as a doorway.

phrases.english: and it is permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: קַרְפֵּף יוֹתֵר מִבֵּית סָאתַיִם שֶׁלֹּא הוּקַּף לְדִירָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: how to repair an enclosure that was not made for living.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Breaking open more than ten אמות and rebuilding down to ten turns the קרפף into one enclosed for living, so carrying is permitted.

steps.title: What if he breaks and rebuilds one cubit at a time?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether the fix still works if he breaks and rebuilds one אמה at a time until more than ten אמות have been redone.
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: if he broke one אמה and fenced one אמה, and broke another אמה and fenced it, until he finished more than ten, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a question (איבעיא) about שמואל's fix. This sets up the discussion that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this case, there was never one open gap of more than ten at the same moment. The question is whether the fix needs a real gap of more than ten, or whether rebuilding more than ten אמות of wall in total is enough.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was raised before them
He broke one אמה and fenced one אמה

phrases.english: They raised a question:
If he broke one cubit and fenced one cubit
and broke another cubit and fenced it,
until he completed more than ten, what is the law?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ: פָּרַץ אַמָּה וְגָדַר אַמָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the limits of שמואל's fix from step 13.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does breaking and rebuilding little by little, adding up to more than ten אמות, work like one big breach of more than ten?

steps.title: The wall question matches a known utensil rule
steps.stepSummary: The responder links the one-אמה-at-a-time wall question to the משנה about the size of a hole that makes a homeowner's utensil טהור.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Isn't this the same issue as what we learned in a משנה: all utensils of homeowners, their measure is the size of pomegranates.
steps.whatsHappening: The responder does not give a yes-or-no answer yet. He points to a similar topic, utensils that become טהור through a hole, to set up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A homeowner's wooden utensil stops being a utensil, and so becomes טהור, once it has a hole the size of a pomegranate. That rule is about one big opening. So it raises the same question as the wall: what if the big opening is made in small pieces?

keyTerms.meaning: Isn't this what we learned (in a משנה)?
Pomegranate (a size measure for a hole)

phrases.english: He said to him: Isn't this what we learned:
All utensils of homeowners,
phrases.notes: Wooden utensils that became impure.

phrases.english: their measure is the size of pomegranates.
phrases.notes: A hole this big ends their status as a utensil, so they become pure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to the Step 14 question by finding a parallel case.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Not a final answer by itself. The question is shown to be the same as an issue about utensils with pomegranate-sized holes, which is settled in step 19.

steps.title: חזקיה asks about small holes that add up
steps.stepSummary: חזקיה asks: if a utensil gets an olive-sized hole that is sealed, then another, and so on until the holes total a pomegranate size, is it טהור?
steps.simpleTranslation: And חזקיה asked: if a utensil was pierced with a hole big enough for an olive to pass through, and he sealed it, and then it was pierced again with an olive-sized hole and he sealed it, until the holes added up to the size for a pomegranate to pass through, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: This is חזקיה's famous question. It is exactly the utensil version of the wall question from Step 14.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each small hole was sealed before the next one opened. So at no single moment was there a pomegranate-sized hole. The question is whether the total of all the small holes counts as one big hole.

keyTerms.meaning: Big enough for an olive to pass through

steps.confusionAlert: Do not picture one hole slowly growing bigger. Each olive-sized hole was fully closed before the next one was made. That is why this is a real question.

phrases.english: And Chizkiya asked:
It was pierced with an olive-sized hole, and he sealed it,
and then it was pierced again with an olive-sized hole, and he sealed it,
until the holes added up to pomegranate size. What is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the dilemma that the Step 15 parallel points to.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Do small sealed holes that add up to pomegranate size make the utensil טהור, the same way one big hole would?

steps.title: רבי יוחנן cites the case of a sandal fixed one strap at a time
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן reminds חזקיה of his own teaching: a sandal with one strap broken and fixed stays טמא מדרס, but once the second strap is also broken and fixed, it is no longer a source of מדרס.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said to him: Rebbe, you taught us: a sandal that had one of its straps break, and he fixed it, is still טמא מדרס. If the second strap broke and he fixed it, it is טהור from מדרס, but it is טמא with מגע מדרס.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן, חזקיה's student, brings a teaching from חזקיה himself to answer the question. In the sandal case, separate repairs made one after another added up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Fixing one strap leaves the sandal the same object, so it keeps its strong מדרס impurity. Once both straps have been replaced, even one at a time, it counts as a new sandal and loses its מדרס status. It only keeps a weaker impurity, from having touched the old impure sandal. The lesson is that changes made one after another can add up, which suggests the small holes, and the wall, should add up too.

keyTerms.meaning: Impure from a זב treading on it, a strong source of impurity
Impurity from touching a מדרס object, a weaker level

steps.whyThisMatters: This gives a real source for the idea that changes made in stages can add up to one full change. That idea is what the wall question and חזקיה's question both depend on.

phrases.aramaic: וַאֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: רַבִּי, שָׁנִיתָה לָנוּ:
phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan said to him: Master, you taught us:
A sandal that had one of its straps break
and he fixed it: it is still impure with midras impurity.
phrases.notes: It is still the same sandal.

phrases.english: If the second strap broke and he fixed it:
it is pure from midras impurity,
phrases.notes: Now it counts as a new item.

phrases.english: but it is impure from contact with midras.
phrases.notes: It touched the earlier impure sandal.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַאֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: רַבִּי, שָׁנִיתָה לָנוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a proof to settle חזקיה's question from Step 16.
steps.raayaObject: That small changes made one after another can add up to one full change, so the olive-sized holes would add up to a pomegranate-sized hole.
steps.raayaSupportSource: חזקיה's own teaching about a sandal whose two straps were broken and fixed one at a time.

steps.title: Why should the second strap matter more than the first?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן reminds חזקיה of the question he himself once raised about the sandal. Why does fixing the first strap leave the sandal טמא, but fixing the second strap makes it lose its status?
steps.simpleTranslation: And you said about this: What is different about the first strap? You say the sandal stays טמא because the second strap is still whole. But when the second strap breaks, the first strap is still standing, since it was repaired!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן is still quoting חזקיה's own teaching. Here he recalls the difficulty חזקיה raised about the sandal ruling. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the first strap breaks and is fixed, the original second strap is still there, so it makes sense that the sandal is the same sandal. When the second strap breaks, the repaired first strap is 'standing' too. So why should the sandal now lose its status? This question pushes toward a new idea: what matters is whether anything original is left.

keyTerms.meaning: What is different? (asks why two cases are treated differently)

steps.confusionAlert: This question is not a new attack on רבי יוחנן. It is part of the quote from חזקיה's own earlier teaching, which רבי יוחנן is reminding him of.

phrases.english: And you said about it:
phrases.notes: 'You' means חזקיה; רבי יוחנן is quoting him.

phrases.english: What is different about the first strap —
that the second one is still intact?
phrases.notes: That is the reason the sandal stays טמא after the first repair.

phrases.english: With the second, too, the first one is intact!
phrases.notes: The first strap was already fixed, so it is 'standing.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבי יוחנן's reminder of חזקיה's sandal teaching by recalling the difficulty raised on it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The sandal ruling that only the second strap's repair removes מדרס status.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both repairs leave one strap 'standing,' so there seems to be no reason to treat them differently.

steps.title: New faces have come here, for the sandal and the utensil alike
steps.stepSummary: חזקיה had answered his own question: after both straps are replaced, the sandal is a new object. רבי יוחנן applies this to the utensil. Once the sealed holes add up to a pomegranate, it too is a new object and is טהור.
steps.simpleTranslation: And you told us about it: 'New faces have come here,' meaning it is a new item. Here too, with the utensil, new faces have come here.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן finishes quoting חזקיה's answer about the sandal. Then he uses that same answer to settle חזקיה's question about the utensil with many patched holes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once every original strap has been replaced, nothing of the old sandal's key parts is left, so it counts as a new sandal. In the same way, if small sealed holes add up to a pomegranate-sized area, that whole area is new. So the utensil is no longer the one that became טמא. The repairs coming one at a time does not stop them from adding up.

keyTerms.meaning: 'New faces have come here': the object has become a new item
Here too (applies the same logic to the current case)

steps.whyThisMatters: The idea of פנים חדשות shows that a series of small changes can add up and give an object a brand-new halachic identity. This is the key to the one-אמה-at-a-time wall question.

phrases.english: And you told us about it:
New faces have come here.
phrases.notes: The sandal with both straps replaced is a new object.

phrases.english: Here too,
phrases.notes: With the utensil that has many patched holes.

phrases.english: new faces have come here.
phrases.notes: So the utensil is טהור.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַאֲמַרְתְּ לַן עֲלַהּ: פָּנִים חֲדָשׁוֹת בָּאוּ לְכָאן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the answer to the step 18 question and applies it to חזקיה's utensil question from step 16.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether olive-sized sealed holes that add up to a pomegranate make the utensil טהור.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Yes. Just like the sandal, the new parts add up and make it a new object, so it is טהור.

steps.title: חזקיה's amazed praise of רבי יוחנן
steps.stepSummary: חזקיה is so impressed that he says about רבי יוחנן either 'this is not a human being' or 'this is what a real person should be.' The one-step-at-a-time approach is now confirmed, including for the wall.
steps.simpleTranslation: He exclaimed about him: 'This is not a human being!' Some say he exclaimed: 'This is what a true human being is like!'
steps.whatsHappening: The discussion closes with חזקיה praising רבי יוחנן for solving his question using חזקיה's own teaching. Two versions of the praise are given.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The praise shows the question is fully settled. Small repairs that add up count as one big change. By extension, שמואל's wall fix from step 13 also works if done one אמה at a time (the question raised in step 14), as long as the total passes ten אמות.

keyTerms.meaning: He exclaimed about him (literally: called out about him)
This is not a human being (he is like an angel)
This is what a true person is like

steps.whatToRemember: Changes made bit by bit still add up. Patching a utensil one hole at a time until the patches reach a pomegranate makes it טהור. In the same way, rebuilding a קרפף wall one אמה at a time until more than ten אמות are redone works for שמואל's fix.

phrases.english: He exclaimed about him:
This is not a human being.
phrases.notes: He is like an angel.

phrases.english: Some say:
This is what a true person is like.

steps.triggerLanguage: קָרֵי עֲלֵיהּ: לֵית דֵּין בַּר אִינָשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the exchange with praise, confirming the answer.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Repairs done step by step add up. This settles the question about rebuilding the wall one אמה at a time: it works.

steps.title: רב כהנא: in a yard behind the houses, carry only four אמות
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא rules that in a רחבה behind houses, one may carry only within four אמות. Some explain this as a fenced storage yard larger than בית סאתים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא said: In a yard that is behind the houses, one may carry only within four אמות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new statement from רב כהנא about a yard behind houses. This opens a new discussion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One explanation is that this yard is fenced but used only for storage, not for living, and is bigger than בית סאתים. Because of that, it does not get the full status of a private domain. So carrying there is limited to four אמות, much like in a כרמלית.

keyTerms.meaning: Four אמות, the basic personal carrying space

phrases.english: Rav Kahana said:
A yard that is behind the houses —
phrases.notes: This yard was used for storage and was larger than בית סאתים.

phrases.english: one may not carry in it
except within four cubits.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב כָּהֲנָא: רְחָבָה שֶׁאֲחוֹרֵי הַבָּתִּים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the wall discussion ends, though it stays on the theme of enclosed areas not used for living.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In a רחבה behind houses, carrying is allowed only within four אמות.

steps.title: A doorway from the house permits the whole area
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן rules that if a doorway was opened from the house into the large fenced area, one may carry in all of it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב נחמן said: If he opened a doorway to it, it is permitted to carry in all of it. The doorway makes it permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן adds to the previous ruling about the רחבה behind houses. If the area has a doorway from the house, one may carry in all of it, not just four אמות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The area is larger than בית סאתים, so normally it does not count as enclosed for living. A doorway from the house shows the area is tied to the home and used together with it. That link gives it the status of a place enclosed for living.

keyTerms.meaning: In all of it (the whole area)

phrases.english: And Rav Nachman said:
If he opened a doorway to it (from the house),
it is permitted to carry in all of it,
the doorway permits it.
phrases.notes: The doorway links the area to the house, so it counts as used for living.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a way to permit the רחבה that רב כהנא limited to four אמות.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A doorway from the house into the large fenced area permits carrying in the whole area.

steps.title: Only if the doorway came before the fence
steps.stepSummary: The ruling applies only when the doorway was opened first and the fence was built afterward, not the other way around.
steps.simpleTranslation: We only said this when he opened the doorway and afterward fenced the area. But if he fenced it first and afterward opened the doorway, it is not permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא limits רב נחמן's ruling. The order matters: doorway first, then fence, is permitted. Fence first, then doorway, is not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the doorway already existed, the fence was clearly built to serve the house, so the enclosure was made for living. If the fence came first, it was put up for some other purpose. Opening a doorway later does not change why the fence was built.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the doorway alone always works. What counts is why the fence was built, and that depends on which came first.

phrases.english: And we said this only
where he opened the doorway and afterward fenced it in,
but if he fenced it in and afterward opened the doorway — no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows רב נחמן's ruling to a specific order of events.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The doorway permits carrying only if it came before the fence.

steps.title: Why say the obvious case?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if the doorway came first and the fence later, of course it is permitted. Why state it?
steps.simpleTranslation: If he opened the doorway and afterward fenced it in, that is obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ruling as too obvious to need saying. It is setting up an answer that will show a hidden case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the doorway was already there, the fence was plainly made to serve the house. So the permission seems self-evident. The גמרא assumes a teacher would not bother stating something so obvious.

phrases.english: Opened and afterward fenced in — that is obvious!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the need to state the permitted case from the previous step.
steps.kashyaTarget: The statement that 'opened then fenced' is permitted.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: When the doorway already existed, the fence clearly served the house, so stating the permission adds nothing.

steps.title: The case of a threshing floor in the area
steps.stepSummary: The ruling is needed where there is a threshing floor in the area. One might think the doorway was made only for the threshing floor, so the גמרא teaches that the whole area is still permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is needed only where there is a threshing floor in it. You might have said he made the doorway only for the threshing floor. So it teaches us that it is still permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the 'it's obvious' challenge. It shows a case where the ruling is not obvious: the area contains a threshing floor.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a threshing floor there, one could think the doorway was opened only to reach the threshing floor, not to use the whole area for living. רב נחמן teaches that the doorway still makes the whole area permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: It is needed only for (a special case)
With the intention of / for the sake of

steps.whatToRemember: A doorway from the house that existed before the fence permits carrying in the whole large area, even if there is a threshing floor in it.

phrases.aramaic: לָא צְרִיכָא, דְּאִית בֵּיהּ בֵּי דָרֵי.
phrases.english: It is needed only where there is a threshing floor in it.
You might have said:
He made the doorway with the threshing floor in mind.
So it teaches us (that it is still permitted).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the פשיטא by finding a case where the ruling is needed.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Case limitation (לא צריכא): the ruling is needed for a special scenario.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The doorway was opened only for the threshing floor, so the area would not count as enclosed for living.
steps.terutzMaskana: The doorway still makes the whole area permitted.

steps.title: The רבנן's first view: a flooded area is like seeds
steps.stepSummary: A קרפף larger than בית סאתים, enclosed for living, became filled with water. The רבנן first assume water is like seeds, so carrying is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: A קרפף larger than בית סאתים that was enclosed for living and then filled with water: the רבנן thought to say it is like seeds, and carrying is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new case and gives the רבנן's first opinion. This step sets up the next step, which will reject it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier we learned that if most of a קרפף is sown with seeds, it is no longer seen as a living area, so carrying is forbidden. Trees do not cancel its living status. The רבנן think water, like seeds, makes the place unfit for living.

keyTerms.meaning: A fenced enclosure outside the home, like a storage yard
An area of two סאה of seed, about 5,000 square אמות
Enclosed for the purpose of living

steps.confusionAlert: 'סבור רבנן למימר' means 'the scholars thought at first.' It signals an initial view that is about to be overturned. It is not the final halacha. These רבנן are simply the scholars in the study hall. They are NOT the רבנן who argue with רבי שמעון in step 5.

phrases.english: A karpef larger than two beit se'a
that was enclosed for living and became filled with water,
the Rabbis thought to say
it is like seeds — and it is forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new case about a large enclosed area losing its living status.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Initial view: water is like seeds, so the flooded קרפף is forbidden for carrying.

steps.title: רבא's view: water is like trees, so it is permitted
steps.stepSummary: רב אבא reports in the name of רבא that water is like planted trees, so carrying in the flooded קרפף stays permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אבא, father of רב, son of רב משרשיא, said to them: This is what we say in the name of רבא: Water is like plantings, and it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אבא rejects the רבנן's first view by quoting רבא. Water does not cancel the living status, so carrying stays permitted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Seeds ruin a place for living, but trees do not, because people enjoy and use them. Water is also useful to the people living there, so it is like trees. The קרפף keeps its status as enclosed for living.

keyTerms.meaning: Are similar to / are treated like

steps.whatToRemember: A קרפף enclosed for living that filled with water is treated like one planted with trees, not seeds. Carrying in it remains permitted.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows the test for 'enclosed for living': anything that still serves the residents, like trees or water, does not cancel the status.

phrases.english: Rav Abba said to them,
father of Rav, son of Rav Mesharshiya:
This is what we say in the name of Rava:
Water is like plantings, and it is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Overturns the רבנן's first view from the previous step.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Fully rejects comparing water to seeds.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Water does not make the place unfit for living. It benefits the residents, like trees.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Water is like plantings, so the flooded קרפף stays permitted for carrying.
